      <title>Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie</link>
      <description><p>Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families</p><p>The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.</p><p>The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">found the cult leader guilty</a> of the crimes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/kenyan-doomsday-sect-leader-jailed-murders-paul-mackenzie">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/06/anc-faces-defeat-south-african-local-elections</link>
      <description><p>Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result</p><p>The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted.</p><p>Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 20:35:13 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>France Unbowed’s Mélenchon unveils ‘A Shared Future’ manifesto ahead of 2027 presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261107-france-unbowed-s-m%C3%A9lenchon-unveils-a-shared-future-manifesto-ahead-of-2027-presidential-race</link><description>
“We are facing a crisis of human civilisation. And we are going to win.”
 
A defiant Jean-Luc Mélenchon was in fighting mood today as he presented his presidential manifesto at Le Bourget, north of Paris. 
 
It is his fourth bid for the French presidency, and he has chosen a venue steeped in left-wing campaign history: the site of François Hollande's famous 2012 rally.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8c2f3754-dad1-11f1-9297-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RH26W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8c2f3754-dad1-11f1-9297-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RH26W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a332b17e-dae5-11f1-a9b9-0f67a89ddb43</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 19:58:43 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><title>🔴 Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot to try to form government</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261107-israeli-president-picks-netanyahu-s-rival-eisenkot-to-try-to-form-government</link><description></description><guid isPermaLink="false">cc39c81c-dae2-11f1-be28-718acff9ff28</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 19:38:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Eisenkot to try to form government</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261107-israeli-president-picks-netanyahu-s-rival-eisenkot-to-try-to-form-government</link><description>
Israeli President Isaac Herzog picked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to try to form a government, he said in a statement Saturday. Last month's parliamentary elections left neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a clear path to building a majority.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b98cb8f6-dae1-11f1-8c71-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T234936Z-337143780-RC2ZBOAVPW2L-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b98cb8f6-dae1-11f1-8c71-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T234936Z-337143780-RC2ZBOAVPW2L-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">75d30d4e-dae2-11f1-8579-699531bb8af2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 19:37:14 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b98cb8f6-dae1-11f1-8c71-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-27T234936Z-337143780-RC2ZBOAVPW2L-RTRMADP-3-ISRAEL-ELECTION.jpg">© Shir Torem, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>'We must change everything': French far-left leader Mélenchon launches presidential programme</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261107-we-must-change-everything-french-far-left-leader-m%C3%A9lenchon-launches-presidential-programme</link><description>
Veteran leftist Jean-Luc Mélenchon formally announced his plan to raise France's minimum wage, cap prices for essential foods and restore the country's retirement age to 60 in a speech launching his 2027 presidential election programme on Saturday. Polls currently indicate that he is the left wing's strongest contender against far-right candidate Marine Le Pen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d0ee97ac-dace-11f1-b377-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261107-165034-175553-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d0ee97ac-dace-11f1-b377-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261107-165034-175553-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d6a95e66-dace-11f1-b324-1db8c4783b3f</guid><pubDate>Sat, 07 Nov 2026 17:30:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France investigating if bogus bomb threats against airlines linked to 'foreign powers'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261107-france-investigating-if-bogus-bomb-threats-against-airlines-linked-to-foreign-powers</link><description>

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before ]]>

On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years!

The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water.

Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites.

Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006.

Why it mattered

As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions.

"The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe.

Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years.

]]> <![CDATA[ Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission ]]> We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission.

Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027.

The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life."

Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024.

NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet.

Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens, which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface.

For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017, providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA.

"Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission. Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments."

Dragonfly's goals include learning more about prebiotic chemistry, or the conditions prior to life arising in a location; figuring out if Titan had habitable conditions in the past; and looking for "chemical indicators" of life based on water or hydrocarbons.

]]> <![CDATA[ Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games ]]> After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games.

With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences.

It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories.

Now this is podracing!

A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious.

Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day.

The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with.

Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer.

It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger.

The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about.

Big, medium, or small, players will react positively to experiences that really feel genuine and aren't brought down by tacked-on systems or monetization. Ubisoft's Massive Entertainment also got it right with Star Wars Outlaws, but that ambitious open-world title — hardly a fresh pitch nowadays — also faced high sales expectations due to an inevitably gigantic production budget.

Do or do not. There is no try.

Allowing Star Wars to get weirder and more specific could also help the movie and TV side of things. We know Star Wars has finally locked in clearer big-screen plans for the coming years, and with Disney Plus TV series being seemingly scaled down and targeting more distinct stories better suited for a non-theatrical medium, the crowds' responses to Lucasfilm Games' wins shouldn't be overlooked.

You can't manufacture a viral character like Biddy Blas, arguably Star Wars' most popular new character since Grogu's debut in 2019. It just happens. And it happens naturally if Star Wars is allowed to explore the weird corners of a galaxy.

Devoid of ties to the larger canon and set away from the Imperial era, Galactic Racer makes the post-war period richer by going smaller. It's a reminder of much of the promise introduced by The Mandalorian's first season, before it became distractingly "relevant" to the larger saga.

Even the Clone Wars-set Zero Company keeps things relatively low-profile. Yes, major characters like Anakin Skywalker make cameos, but they don't rob the A-Team and Suicide Squad-inspired tale of camaraderie and subterfuge of its valuable independence. Sure, hits like Andor and Rogue One were obvious inspirations for its tone, but the story stands alone, allowing even Star Wars newcomers to jump in and enjoy it with minimal context.

At a time when giant decades-old franchises often struggle to recruit new fans, the last two Star Wars games reinforce the property's new direction in a medium that can reach more potential Padawans than any other.

The good trick? Just allowing Star Wars to be fresh and smaller — and with no homework required — from time to time. In turn, the larger stories on the horizon will be stronger with the Force.

"If NASA is going to be doing deep-space missions, complicated missions, [we should] launch at least once a year and get as much out of it as you can for taking the risk and spending the taxpayer dollars and building towards something greater," Isaacman added. On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day.

Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star."

At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it.

Why it mattered

The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572, is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star.

While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky.

"The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia, was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004. "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova."

"This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time.

Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis, or the Blaze Star, the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so.

]]> <![CDATA[ AST SpaceMobile announces new 'Blacklift' rocket, targets 2028 launch debut ]]> Another new private rocket is in the works.

AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028.

The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron, a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers. Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff.

"The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today.

"This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added.

Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites, which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite.

BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9, Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift.

The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace, to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly.

Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage.

Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile.

"The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement.

The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement.

Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. Each launch will therefore be able to loft up to five BlueBird satellites, according to today's announcement. (For perspective: The Falcon 9's LEO lift capacity is about 25 tons.)

BlueBirds will continue going up while AST SpaceMobile gets Blacklift ready to fly: The company already holds contracts with other providers to launch more than 100 of the satellites over the course of 2027 and 2028.

The launch landscape will likely be very different when Blacklift, Big Iron and other new rockets come online. SpaceX has said that it plans to phase out the Falcon 9, as well as its Falcon Heavy heavy lifter, after its Starship megarocket gets up and running.

SpaceX has indicated that it will prioritize launches of its own satellites with Starship. And there will be a lot of them to loft — 100,000 Starlink V3 satellites and a million Starmind AI data centers, company founder and CEO Elon Musk has suggested.

In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight.

It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky.

In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew.

What goes up, must come down

After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition.

So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight.

It's not E.T. It's only Venus.

These are the first pair of smart binoculars that can identify targets in the night sky, such as planets, stars and deep space objects.

The build is solid and while they aren't the most lightweight binoculars, the body is hiding that extra technology that enables the AR overlay in the right hand lens. Each pair ships with a soft carry case, a padded neck strap, a USB-C cable and rubber caps for the eyepieces and lenses.

Pre-order the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars for $1,499 / £1,299

I would highly recommend setting these binoculars up in the daytime, as you definitely need a few minutes to get used to the controls and to perform the diopter adjustment. After powering on, all I had to do was connect the model to the Unistellar app, which recognised the device easily and then watch the onboarding videos. Unistellar also recommends performing a 360-degree calibration before your first use to help ensure the best performance.

You need to have location services set to "always" for the Unistellar app so that it can work out your exact location and give you an accurate reading on the augmented reality (AR) display for locations of night sky targets and landmarks.

I haven't had chance to use the night mode on these binoculars yet, thanks to cloudy skies, but I did use the topographical identification and was impressed with the ease of identifying landmarks around my local area. Besides the night and daytime modes, there is also a navigation mode which displays your cardinal direction alongside degrees of your azimuth and elevation angles.

I had a chance to try out the target lock feature on a geographical landmark with a friend and they found the target easily via the indicator on the AR display. The issue with swapping between two people is that the diopter adjustment only be accurate for one person and I can imagine that constantly changing it during field observation would be annoying. My friend also had to adjust the focus wheel to get the AR overlay sharp enough to read but it was a minor inconvenience.

The controls are intuitive and easy to use once you are used to the placement on the top panel. On the left you have the "next" button for advancing a guided tour to the next target, the "target lock" button and the "mode" button for cycling through the different display modes. On the right is the calibration button for adjusting the augmented reality (AR) display against your real-world view and the power button, which doubles up as a switch to turn the AR display on and off.

I'm looking forward to putting the Unistellar Envisions through their paces as I spend more time with them and get some clear skies to try them out on some stars. I think that these are going to be a great tool for learning my way around the night sky, as well as being invaluable when trying to teach others about constellations and targets. With extra functionality expected in future software updates and a plan to allow third-party app development in 2027, I am excited about the possibilities of the exciting new world of smart binoculars.

   <title>Právníci kritizují dětský certifikát: Se záměrem souhlasíme, s provedením ne</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/cesko-detsky-certifikat-kritizuji-pravnici-proc/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Dětský certifikát, tedy evidence skutečností důležitých pro práci s dětmi, je zvláštní výpis z rejstříku trestů, jenž má zabránit práci s dětmi osobám odsouzeným za vybrané závažné trestné činy. Stát jej zavádí jako preventivní nástroj na ochranu dětí, protože dosavadní zákazy práce s dětmi byly časově omezené a ne vždy dokázaly zabránit návratu rizikových osob do profesí, kde přicházejí do kontaktu s nezletilými. Dětský certifikát byl načten do novely trestního zákoníku jako pozměňovací návrh skupiny poslanců napříč politickými stranami. Kritikům se nelíbí některé nedodělky a nelogičnosti v zákoně nebo to, že neměří „stejným metrem“. Dodávají ale, že s principe m dětského certifikátu souhlasí, připomínky mají pouze k provedení. Některá opatření kritizuje i současný ministr spravedlnosti Jeroným Tejc (za ANO) či bývalá ministryně spravedlnosti Eva Decroix (ODS).</description>

V SOBOTU 7. LISTOPADU VYRAZÍ Z DRÁŽĎAN PARNÍ VLAK NA MOLDAVU!

Železniční muzeum Dresden-Altstadt a spolek Flügelradtouristik pořádají mimořádnou jízdu historického vlaku s oddílovými osobními vozy a jídelním vozem.

Z Drážďan vyrazí v 6:30 s německou parní lokomotivou 35 1097 přes Rumburk a Děčín do Mostu. Zde převezme vlak česká parní lokomotiva 433.001 „Skaličák“, které bude na horské trati pomáhat dieselová lokomotiva.

Most 12:00 – Osek město 12:32 – Dubí 13:22 – Moldava 14:09. Zpět z Moldavy vlak odjede v 15:20 přes Dubí, Louku u Litvínova a Teplice do Drážďan. Část historické soupravy zamíří také do Žatce, města chmele a piva.

Souprava na nádraží doplnila vodu (výpomoc poskytly dva vozy JSDH Brtníky), a posádka provedla na mašině nutný servis (trochu mne zaskočily dva pytle písku, ale má to logické vysvětlení).

Ve skupině jsme nejprve porazili pozdějšího vítěze, rumburskou obchodku 2:1, když naše góly zařídili Hlavsa a Průša. Poté jsme přesvědčivě zválcovali Mariánskou poměrem 5:0. Turnaj se hrál systémem 3 + 1. Každý tým se utkal s každým soupeřem dvoukolově, přičemž jedno utkání trvalo 2 × 8 minut. Na turnaji se představily tři týmy – ZŠ Východní, Centrum dětí a mládeže Česká Kamenice a naše škola. Každý tým tak odehrál celkem čtyři utkání. Vítězný tým turnaje postoupí do krajského finále.

Tentokrát nám soupeř porážku oplatil a po dramatickém průběhu jsme prohráli nejtěsnějším rozdílem 2:3. Jelikož i ZŠ Východní zvítězila nad Českou Kamenicí, bylo před závěrečným utkáním jasné, že o vítězi turnaje rozhodne počet vstřelených branek proti tomuto soupeři.

Po většinu turnaje nás v brance skvěle držel Adam Reichert, který několika výbornými zákroky podržel tým v nejtěžších chvílích. Pro rozhodující utkání jsme však zvolili odvážný taktický tah.
